newsitem.title: USA: Munis may be part of corporate welfare reform - PSA.
newsitem.headline: Munis may be part of corporate welfare reform - PSA.

text.p: The treatment of municipal bonds under the federal tax code could be lumped in with plans to reform how corporations are taxed, a municipal bond lobbyist said Wednesday.

Micah Green, head of Public Securities Association's Washington office, said municipal bonds could be included in proposals to eliminate tax loopholes geared for corporations. He spoke at a Grant's Municipal Bond Observor conference here.
Green said that municipal bonds could be adversely affected by corporate welfare reform proposals designed to help balance the federal budget.

Municipal bond financings, like industrial development bonds, private activity bonds, and stadium bonds, which could benefit private corporations, could be eliminated as tax reformers seek to raise revenues by closing tax loopholes.

Looking at other tax issues that will face Congress next year, Green pointed out that flat tax proposals have not gone away. "The talk is not dead. The talk is still out there." The impact of a flat tax on the municipal bond market still is being studied by a PSA task force.

Muncipal bonds could be affected by two possible approachs to tax reform, a fundamental or an incremental effort, but they might fare better under fundamental reform, which might produce some interesting effects, Green said.
For example, eliminating taxes on savings and investment income might create an international marketplace for municipal bonds.
But under incremental tax reform, muncipal bonds could be relegated to competing with other special interests seeking to defend their tax preferences, Green said.
